    StartersThe breadless bread plateCultured butter, whipped ricotta and olive oil with warm sourdough, bread includedHow to make it125g cultured butter3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil150g ricotta1 box sea salt flakes1 sourdough loafWhip the ricotta until light.Set out the butter, oil and ricotta in separate dishes, each with a few salt flakes.Because you're not on that island, warm the sourdough and serve it with them.Raw scallop with finger limeThinly sliced raw scallops with lime, finger lime pearls, olive oil and sea saltHow to make it300g scallops1 lime2 finger limes1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil1 box sea salt flakesChill the plates.Slice the scallops very thin and lay on the plates.Dress with lime juice, finger lime pearls, a few drops of oil and sea salt.Etched tortillas with chipotle salsaThe tortillas with the guests' secrets printed on themHow to make itAs written, serves 4Warm corn tortillas charred on a dry pan, with a smoky charred tomato and chipotle salsa, smashed avocado with lime and crumbled feta.Char 4 tomatoes, half a white onion and 2 garlic cloves in a dry pan until blackened in spots.Blitz with 1 chipotle in adobo, a handful of coriander, lime juice and salt.Mash 2 avocados with lime and salt.Warm 16 small corn tortillas in a hot dry pan for 30 seconds a side until lightly charred and keep wrapped in a tea towel.Serve with the salsa, avocado and 80g crumbled feta.Island oysters with sea lettuce granitaDo not eat. Taste, as Chef says.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsThe cheeseburgerSmashed beef patties with American cheese, onion and pickles, crinkle cut friesHow to make it800g beef chuck mince8 slices of American cheese1 brown onion1 jar dill pickles4 burger buns1kg potatoes2 L vegetable oilCut the potatoes crinkle style and fry in the vegetable oil at 140°C until soft, then drain.Shape the beef mince into eight thin patties and slice the onion and pickles.Smash the patties on a smoking griddle and add the cheese.Toast the buns and stack two patties per bun with onion and pickles.Fry the chips again at 185°C until crisp. Wrap one to take home.Hawthorn lamb rack with celeriac puréeA tasting menu main, without the theatreHow to make itAs written, serves 4Lamb rack roasted pink and carved into cutlets, on silky celeriac purée with charred baby leeks and a glossy red wine jus.Simmer a peeled, diced celeriac in 400ml milk for 20 minutes, then blitz with 40g butter until silky.Season 2 lamb racks, sear fat side down, then roast at 200°C to 56°C inside, about 15 minutes, and rest 10 minutes.Blanch 8 baby leeks for 2 minutes and char in a hot pan.Reduce 200ml red wine with a shallot by half, add 300ml beef stock and reduce until glossy, then whisk in 20g butter.SweetsCampfire s'mores tartChocolate ganache in a cookie crust, topped with torched meringueHow to make it250g digestive biscuits100g butter200g dark chocolate200ml thickened cream3 eggs150g caster sugarCrush the biscuits, mix with melted butter and press into a tart tin.Heat the cream, pour over the chocolate and stir to a ganache. Pour into the case.Chill until set.Whisk the egg whites with the sugar over hot water, then beat stiff.Spread on top and torch until blistered.DrinksHawthorn smoked rosemary negroniGin, bitter aperitivo and sweet vermouth with a smoking rosemary sprigHow to make it120ml gin120ml bitter red aperitivo120ml sweet vermouth1 bunch rosemary1 orange4 large ice cubesStir the gin, aperitivo and vermouth with ice for 20 seconds, in batches.Strain over a large ice cube in each tumbler.Light the tip of a rosemary sprig until it smokes, blow it out and lay it across the glass with a twist of orange peel.Sommelier's dry island rieslingPairs well with Tyler's mouthfeel speech.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
